items.summary:
Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation

OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents. Agents are most useful when they can read files, install packages, call APIs, and use credentials. OpenShell gives them tha

confirmed_facts.text: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents.

confirmed_facts.text: Agents are most useful when they can read files, install packages, call APIs, and use credentials.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Agents are most useful when they can read files, install packages, call APIs, and use credentials.

confirmed_facts.text: OpenShell gives them that capability without giving them unrestricted access to your data, secrets, or network.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: OpenShell gives them that capability without giving them unrestricted access to your data, secrets, or network.

confirmed_facts.text: You declare what each agent can touch in a policy, and OpenShell enforces it.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: You declare what each agent can touch in a policy, and OpenShell enforces it.

confirmed_facts.text: OpenShell governs what agents can do in two ways: it instruments the kernel to enforce policy on every file access, system call, and network connection at runtime, and it uses formal verification to check what a policy change would allow before it is applied.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: OpenShell governs what agents can do in two ways: it instruments the kernel to enforce policy on every file access, system call, and network connection at runtime, and it uses formal verification to check what a policy change would allow before it is applied.

confirmed_facts.text: Kernel controls confine which files it can access and which system calls it can make, and every network connection passes through a policy check before it leaves the sandbox.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Kernel controls confine which files it can access and which system calls it can make, and every network connection passes through a policy check before it leaves the sandbox.

items.title: Nvidia's role as AI financier faces first big test as neoclouds take market hit
items.summary: As Nvidia has gone from chipmaker to industry financier, some investors see the company taking on outsized risk tied to the AI buildout.

confirmed_facts.text: Nvidia's emergence as financier for the global AI buildout is facing its first major stress test as credit markets tighten for key partners.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's emergence as financier for the global AI buildout is facing its first major stress test as credit markets tighten for key partners.

confirmed_facts.text: That's meant taking full advantage of Nvidia's investment grade credit rating and providing backstop guarantees on mega-projects for OpenAI so that buildouts can get funded at lower interest rates.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: That's meant taking full advantage of Nvidia's investment grade credit rating and providing backstop guarantees on mega-projects for OpenAI so that buildouts can get funded at lower interest rates.

confirmed_facts.text: As of its last quarterly financial filing in July, Nvidia had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, in addition to its guarantee on up to $105 billion for chips, land and power at a proposed 10 gigawatt OpenAI data center in Ohio.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: As of its last quarterly financial filing in July, Nvidia had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, in addition to its guarantee on up to $105 billion for chips, land and power at a proposed 10 gigawatt OpenAI data center in Ohio.

confirmed_facts.text: The company signed as a tenant for $20 billion in future data center leases, which will later be assigned to third parties.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: The company signed as a tenant for $20 billion in future data center leases, which will later be assigned to third parties.

confirmed_facts.text: "If the demand for compute doesn't meet these really super lofty expectations, we're going to have a problem," said David Trainer, founder and CEO of financial research firm New Constructs, in an interview.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: "If the demand for compute doesn't meet these really super lofty expectations, we're going to have a problem," said David Trainer, founder and CEO of financial research firm New Constructs, in an interview.
